 San José’s Festival de la Luz Swaps Floats for 10 Giant Balloons This Year
 By The Tico Times 
 November 16, 2026 
 Share 
 Facebook X WhatsApp Email 
 Lindsay Fendt/The Tico Times 
 San José will welcome the Christmas season with one of Costa Rica’s best-loved holiday traditions when the Festival de la Luz returns to the capital on Saturday, December 12, with giant illuminated balloons, marching bands, and live street performances. The Municipality of San José unveiled the 2026 program on Friday, confirming that this year’s parade will feature 10 balloons, 14 marching bands, and six ground-level shows.
 The parade begins at 6 p.m. and will run from Plaza de la Democracia west along Paseo Colón to Torre Mercedes. That is a change from last year’s festival , when the parade looped around La Sabana Park. The biggest difference this year is the absence of floats. The municipality turned to balloons after six public institutions pulled their floats out of the festival in August, a withdrawal Mayor Diego Miranda has attributed to political differences with the central government.
 The balloon lineup includes three blimp-style figures that will float above the route and seven illuminated inflatables. Four of the designs were chosen through a consultation with students from Escuela Metálica and Escuela República del Perú, giving local children a say in the celebration.
 The six ground shows will bring characters, artistic performances, and moments of interaction with the crowd along the route. Bands in the parade are also scheduled to perform at the Band Fest the same day, and a street procession is planned ahead of the main event. Miranda said the municipality wants to offer a renewed experience that brings families together through music, creativity, and entertainment.
 The municipality has not yet released road closures, public transportation arrangements, or security plans for the night. Officials said those details will be published through municipal channels as the date approaches. Last year, streets around the parade area closed from 11 p.m. the night before the festival.
 The Festival de la Luz anchors a wider holiday calendar the municipality calls the Mes de la Luz, or Month of Light. On Monday, November 30, the municipality and the National Power and Light Company (CNFL) will switch on the capital’s Christmas lights at Plaza de la Cultura. Ten districts will also host community Christmas festivals between November 14 and December 20, with music, parades, local businesses, food vendors, recreational activities, and artistic performances.
 The district festivals open Saturday, November 14, at the Zapote Sports Complex, followed by Catedral on Sunday, November 15. The other participating districts are San Francisco, Pavas, Hospital, San Sebastián, Mata Redonda, Merced, La Uruca, and Carmen. Most of the neighborhood festivals run from noon to 8 p.m., though some keep different hours. The last one is scheduled for December 20 at the Aranjuez Sports Complex in Carmen.
